claims.text: This dataset covers 4,203 inpatient stays across 12 months, with a 30-day readmission rate of 9.0%, in-hospital mortality of 2.4%, and an average length of stay of 3.72 days.
Cardiology accounts for the largest share of total charges among all departments, while total charges fell sharply in Oct 2026 compared with Sep 2026.
Cardiology's higher readmissions were caused by poorer care in the department, so its discharge planning should be overhauled.
The dataset contains 4,203 stays from 1,707 patients; Vascular Surgery had only 7 stays, with 2 deaths among its patients.
Cardiology generated the highest total charges ($51,663,189.13), followed by Orthopedics ($33,207,578.70) and General Medicine ($24,167,064.42).

Total charges fell 26.3% from Sep 2026 to Oct 2026; because the data covers only 12 months with no prior-year equivalent, it is not possible to determine whether this is seasonal or a genuine decline.
Per-stay charges vary widely, and three patients were readmitted twice within one week of discharge.

Investigate the drivers of the Oct 2026 drop in total charges before drawing conclusions or adjusting budgets. A 26.3% month-over-month fall is material; confirming whether it is seasonal or structural prevents misinformed planning.

Review the small number of stays with very high charges (up to $827,622.78) to confirm they are coded correctly and assess their effect on departmental totals. Outliers flagged in Total Charges could distort department-level comparisons and financial forecasts.

Risk-adjust the 9.0% readmission rate and 2.4% mortality rate before using them for benchmarking or performance reporting. Crude rates can mislead if case mix differs across departments or time periods.

claims.text: Across 11 months of claims, total paid reached $257,150.19 across 2,668 claims for 403 members, with Northwind Health accounting for the largest share of paid spend and a 9.5% claim denial rate.
Recent service months should be read with caution, as claims continue arriving for roughly three months after service, so apparent drops in late months reflect lag rather than a real trend.
Northwind Health is the largest payer by paid amount at $131,095.83, followed by Summit Mutual at $49,026.14 and Lakeside Care at $38,167.93.

Paid amounts are highly skewed: the median paid per claim line is $23.79 while the mean is $55.32, and values range from -$442.37 to $506.26, with negative values and high-end figures flagged as outliers but kept in the data.
Month-over-month, paid amount fell 6.3%, and the decline should be treated as a settled trend in utilization.
The overall claim denial rate stands at 9.5%; at Crescent Health only 4 members had a claim denied.

Investigate Northwind Health claims for coding patterns or contract terms that explain its outsized paid total relative to other payers. Northwind Health paid total is more than double the next largest payer, making it the primary driver of overall spend.

Review the root causes of the 9.5% claim denial rate by payer and service type to identify where resubmission or process changes could recover revenue. Reducing denials directly increases collected revenue without adding new claims volume.

Audit claim lines with negative paid or allowed amounts to confirm they represent legitimate adjustments rather than data errors. Negative values affect total paid and allowed figures and could distort any downstream cost analysis.
